        source_class: saved_artifact
        path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/conversations/CONV-20260909-5299cf.md
        available_excerpt: "# Harbor 2 — Matter dossier\n\n*Current as of September
          12, 2026*\n\n## Current position\n\nThe Harbor Pay acquisition migration
          needs legal and compliance review before close.\n\nMosaic plans to move
          240,000 consumer accounts and 12,000 business accounts into its app on day
          one after an asset purchase. The plan also assumes Harbor’s licenses can
          support four new states, relies on Harbor’s prior identity checks, changes
          the transaction-monitoring system at close, and starts a $50 welcome offer
          one day later.\n\nThe main obstacle is the lack of confirmed authority for
          Mosaic to provide regulated services in the four Harbor-only states. The
          current licensing research retrieved four sources but did not read or verify
          the controlling passages. The identity-check records, open alerts, suspicious
          activity report history, and monitoring transition also remain unresolved.\n\nThe
          acquisition can close separately from a full migration. However, the saved
          working view is that Mosaic should not launch a regulated service in a state
          without confirmed authority. No final launch decision has been recorded.\n\nThe
          reported close date is Nov 15. Separate matter metadata lists `2026-09-11`
          as a target or requested launch date. The records do not explain this difference.\n\n##
          Decision question\n\nDoes any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration
          need legal review before the Nov 15 close?\n\n## Issues\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
          -->\n### Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
          under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor's MTLs transfer/survive
          the acquisition\n\n**Current answer**\n\nYes. This is a pre-close legal
          review item and a launch gate for the four Harbor-only states. Mosaic should
          not treat Harbor’s money transmitter licenses as assets that automatically
          move to Mosaic in the asset purchase.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe saved
          research position is that the answer must be determined state by state.
          It may depend on the licensed entity, transaction structure, actual funds
          flow, required filings, regulator approval, and whether Harbor remains the
          provider.\n\nThe research retrieved four sources, but no passages were read.
          It therefore does not yet verify an applicable state rule, approval path,
          or regulator position. See the [licensing research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md).\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor
          reportedly holds licenses in 38 states. Mosaic reportedly holds licenses
          in 41 states. The business plans to use or assume Harbor’s licenses in four
          additional markets. The transaction is an asset purchase, and the migration
          would give users one Mosaic account and access to Mosaic’s products.\n\nThese
          facts do not establish that Harbor’s licenses authorize Mosaic after close.
          A bank-held-funds structure remains only a hypothetical. It could change
          the analysis if the bank has the legally important customer, account, transfer,
          settlement, and repayment roles. Custody by a bank alone does not answer
          the question.\n\n**Next step**\n\nInformation and verified legal analysis
          remain open. Identify the four Harbor-only states. For each state, document
          Mosaic’s authority, required transaction filings or approvals, any permitted
          interim operation, the planned funds flow, Harbor’s outstanding obligations,
          and the conditions for license surrender. Regulated launch should remain
          excluded in a state until a lawful route is confirmed.\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045
          -->\n### BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor's prior KYC (with missing
          underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay's independent
          CIP/AML obligations\n\n**Current answer**\n\nLegal and compliance review
          is required before Mosaic relies on Harbor’s prior identity checks without
          re-verification. This issue has not been researched.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe
          saved record identifies Mosaic’s Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money-laundering
          program, including its customer identification program, as the relevant
          framework. No external legal authority has been saved for this issue.\n\nMosaic’s
          own program requirements are also unknown. Compliance has not confirmed
          whether the program permits reliance on another institution’s prior checks.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor’s
          former vendor produced pass/fail results but shut down in 2024. Mosaic does
          not have the underlying documents for users onboarded before 2023. The planned
          migration would give Harbor users access to Mosaic’s full product set without
          new verification.\n\nA pass result does not, by itself, establish that Mosaic
          has the records or legal basis required by its own program. The effect could
          include re-verification, limits on account access, or another documented
          control. The saved material does not determine which response is required.\n\n**Next
          step**\n\nResearch, information, and implementation remain open. Compliance
          must review Mosaic’s written program and the available Harbor records. Legal
          must then determine whether the proposed reliance is permitted and what
          treatment is required for users whose underlying records are missing.\n\n<!--
          issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38 -->\n### SAR and alert handling: obligations
          to review, file, and manage Harbor's ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor
          liability\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe alerts and suspicious activity report
          history require review before migration. Their effect on the transaction
          and post-close duties cannot be assessed while they remain unread. This
          issue has not been researched.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe saved analysis
          identifies federal financial-crime duties and possible successor obligations
          as relevant. No external legal authority has been saved for this issue.\n\n**Application**\n\nDiligence
          found about 40 open alerts and a handful of suspicious activity reports
          from the prior year. None have been reviewed. The records therefore do not
          show the nature or age of the alerts, whether investigations are complete,
          whether filing deadlines may apply, or whether the matters concern users
          scheduled for migration.\n\nAn asset purchase does not establish that all
          duties disappear or transfer. The purchase documents, Harbor’s retained
          duties, Mosaic’s post-close role, and the contents of the files may affect
          the answer.\n\n**Next step**\n\nInformation, research, and a responsibility
          decision remain open. Review the alerts and report history. Create a case
          list showing status, age, required action, responsible entity, records to
          transfer, and treatment after close. Escalate any matter that may affect
          the deal or migration population.\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542
          -->\n### Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
          when the SaaS contract terminates at close\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe
          day-one system change needs compliance review and operational testing before
          migration. The saved record does not establish that monitoring will continue
          without a gap. This issue has not been researched.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe
          relevant saved framework is continuity of Mosaic’s financial-crime monitoring
          controls. No external legal authority has been saved for this issue.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor’s
          monitoring software contract ends at close. The plan is to redirect Harbor’s
          transaction feed to Mosaic’s system on day one. No saved evidence shows
          that the data mapping, alert rules, historical data, system capacity, or
          failure process has been tested.\n\nThis creates a possible monitoring gap
          at the same time that 252,000 accounts move into Mosaic’s app. The open
          Harbor alerts make continuity more important because the new system may
          need historical context and unresolved case data.\n\n**Next step**\n\nEvidence
          and implementation remain open. Complete an end-to-end test that covers
          all Harbor transaction types, data fields, alert generation, case transfer,
          historical access, reconciliation, and failure handling. Document the result
          and any temporary control needed at close.\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66
          -->\n### Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
          money transmission or consumer protection implications\n\n**Current answer**\n\nThe
          offer needs legal review before release. The saved material does not contain
          enough information to determine the required disclosures or other limits.
          This issue has not been researched.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nState money-transmission
          and consumer-protection rules may apply based on the offer’s terms, funds
          flow, eligibility limits, and advertising claims. No external legal authority
          has been saved for this issue.\n\n**Application**\n\nMarketing plans a $50
          bonus on a customer’s first transfer, with launch at close plus one day.
          The offer structure remains unknown. The record does not state who funds
          the bonus, when it becomes payable, whether it can be withdrawn, what transfer
          qualifies, which users or states are eligible, or whether the offer expires.\n\nThe
          campaign also depends on the underlying service being lawfully available.
          Marketing approval cannot solve an unresolved license or migration restriction.\n\n**Next
          step**\n\nInformation and legal analysis remain open. Obtain the complete
          offer terms, customer messages, eligibility rules, funds flow, state scope,
          and complaint process. Review these items before publication and exclude
          any state or customer group that cannot use the underlying service.\n\n##
          Assumptions and record limits\n\nNo additional assumptions are treated as
          confirmed facts.\n\nThe saved record still lists open model assumptions
          about license transfer, KYC sufficiency, and monitoring continuity. This
          dossier does not rely on those assumptions as true. Each is an unresolved
          matter requiring evidence.\n\nThe acquisition structure is now reported
          as an asset purchase. The older assumption that the structure was unknown
          is stale. The bank-held-funds structure remains hypothetical and does not
          change the current direction.\n\n## Next actions\n\nNo open action has a
          recorded owner or due date. The entries below are proposed actions, not
          assigned work.\n\n1. **Proposed — Review Harbor’s open alerts and suspicious
          activity report history.**  \n   **Owner:** Not assigned.  \n   **Date:**
          No date recorded.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Case files, filing history,
          alert age and status, investigation notes, deadlines, user links, and a
          responsibility list for pre- and post-close work.\n\n2. **Proposed — Complete
          the four-state licensing matrix and set launch gates.**  \n   **Owner:**
          Not assigned.  \n   **Date:** No date recorded.  \n   **Evidence needed:**
          Identity of the four states, current licenses, state rules and regulator
          guidance, required filings or approvals, funds-flow documents, purchase
          terms, outstanding obligations, and surrender requirements.\n\n3. **Proposed
          — Decide how Mosaic will satisfy identity-check and recordkeeping duties.**
          \ \n   **Owner:** Not assigned.  \n   **Date:** No date recorded.  \n   **Evidence
          needed:** Mosaic’s written anti-money-laundering and customer identification
          programs, Harbor’s procedures, available customer records, vendor outputs,
          population counts, and a proposed treatment for missing records.\n\n4. **Proposed
          — Test transaction-monitoring continuity.**  \n   **Owner:** Not assigned.
          \ \n   **Date:** No date recorded.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Test results,
          data mapping, rule coverage, case migration, historical access, reconciliation,
          capacity results, and a failure or rollback plan.\n\n5. **Proposed — Review
          the $50 welcome offer before release.**  \n   **Owner:** Not assigned.  \n
          \  **Date:** No date recorded.  \n   **Evidence needed:** Final terms, advertisements,
          eligibility rules, qualifying-transfer definition, state scope, bonus funds
          flow, withdrawal limits, expiration terms, and complaint process.\n\nThe
          only saved work item, **Orient to the request**, was assigned to the Lawyer
          and completed on September 9, 2026. See [WI-20260909-dc797b](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/work-items/WI-20260909-dc797b.md).\n\n##
          Current work product and records\n\n- **Current work product:** No current
          draft or final path is recorded.\n- **Licensing research:** [RES-20260911-0a5f07.md](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n-
          **Reported facts:** [facts.md](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md)\n- **Original
          request:** [request.md](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/request.md)\n- **Prior
          dossier revision:** [DOS-c993ab2326efd727cc3d.md](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/dossier-revisions/DOS-c993ab2326efd727cc3d.md)\n\n<!--
          saved-issue-analysis:start -->\n## Saved issue answers\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
          -->\n### Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
          under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor's MTLs transfer/survive
          the acquisition\n\nDo not rely on transferability without an applicable
          state rule, approval, or written regulator position.\n\nThe answer must
          be determined state by state and must cover more than technical change-of-control
          rules.\n\nThis path is possible only if Harbor remains the real provider
          and the relevant states permit the arrangement. The unified Mosaic account
          design may conflict with that position.\n\nThe result depends on the contracts
          and actual funds flow. Custody alone should not be treated as a licensing
          exemption or transfer mechanism.\n\nResearch saved. 4 sources retrieved;
          0 with passages read.\n\nNext step: Identify the four Harbor-only states
          and complete one matrix covering license authority, transaction filings,
          interim operation, bank custody, outstanding obligations, and license surrender.\n\n<details>\n<summary>Detailed
          analysis</summary>\n\n**Practical answer**\n\n**Do not treat Harbor’s money
          transmitter licenses as assets that move to Mosaic in the asset purchase.**
          Use this closing rule:\n\n> **No confirmed authority means no regulated
          launch by Mosaic in that state.**\n\nThe asset purchase can still close.
          However, Mosaic should not activate regulated services in the four Harbor-only
          states unless one of these conditions is met:\n\n1. Mosaic obtains its own
          license.\n2. The state approves a transfer or other license change.\n3.
          The regulator confirms a lawful interim structure.\n4. Harbor remains the
          real licensed provider under a valid transition plan.\n5. Mosaic blocks
          regulated functions in that state.\n\nThe planned unified Mosaic account
          is important. It suggests that Mosaic, not Harbor, will become the service
          provider. If that is correct, keeping Harbor’s legal entity and licenses
          alive might not give Mosaic authority to operate.\n\n**No verified operative
          authority retrieved.** The collection found the CSBS Model Money Transmission
          Modernization Act and a New York regulator licensing page. However, no exact
          provision about an asset sale, license transfer, interim operation, or custody
          was available for review. Also, a model act is not proof of the law adopted
          in a specific state. The state-specific conclusions below remain conditional.\n\n**Work
          needed before launch**\n\n| Work | Why | Proposed owner | Needed by | Evidence
          to proceed | Fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Identify the four
          Harbor-only states | These states have the clearest authority gap | Licensing
          team | Now | Confirmed license list and covered activities | Block regulated
          functions in those states |\n| Build a matrix for every affected state |
          Transfer, notice, approval, and surrender rules can differ | State regulatory
          counsel | Before the closing conditions are final | Applicable rule, filing
          deadline, regulator response, and license status | Delay migration in the
          affected state |\n| Confirm the post-close service provider | The licensed
          entity must match the actual operating model | Product and deal counsel
          | Before customer notices and account design are final | Contracts, user
          interface, funds-flow diagram, and operating roles | Keep Harbor as the
          actual provider where permitted |\n| Review notices and approvals | An asset
          sale can create separate seller and buyer requirements | Licensing team
          | Before each state deadline | Filing receipts and required approvals or
          non-objections | Make approval a state launch condition |\n| Confirm interim
          operating authority | A pending application should not be assumed to permit
          operation | State regulatory counsel | Before close | Applicable rule or
          written regulator confirmation | Keep Harbor customers segregated or restrict
          transactions |\n| Review partner-bank arrangements | Bank custody does not,
          by itself, establish Mosaic’s licensing position | Payments counsel and
          bank relationship owner | Before balances move | Bank agreements, account
          titles, control rights, reconciliation design, and bank consent | Keep funds
          and obligations in the existing structure |\n| Prepare license run-off and
          surrender plans | Harbor may retain duties for balances, claims, records,
          and reports | Harbor compliance and deal counsel | Before surrender or operational
          shutdown | Regulator-approved plan and continued bonds and financial coverage
          | Keep Harbor licensed and operational longer |\n\n**State notice and approval**\n\nDo
          not search only for a rule called “license transfer.” Review each state
          for:\n\n- sale of substantially all assets;\n- change of control;\n- change
          in business plan;\n- change in licensed activities;\n- assignment of outstanding
          payment obligations;\n- change in responsible persons, locations, or agents;\n-
          license surrender or termination;\n- customer agreement assignment; and\n-
          movement of stored balances or customer funds.\n\nAn asset purchase might
          fall outside a technical “change of control” rule because Harbor’s ownership
          does not change. That does not resolve the issue. Harbor might still need
          a notice or surrender approval. Mosaic might separately need authority before
          it starts the regulated activity.\n\nThe state matrix should distinguish:\n\n-
          notice only;\n- approval before closing;\n- approval before customer migration;\n-
          new license required;\n- operation permitted while an application is pending;\n-
          regulator-approved transition available; and\n- no supported interim path.\n\n**Interim
          operation**\n\nHarbor could remain the licensed provider for a transition
          period. However, the structure must be real, not only contractual language.\n\nA
          supportable structure would normally need to show that:\n\n- Harbor remains
          responsible to customers.\n- Customer terms name Harbor as the provider.\n-
          Harbor controls the regulated activity as required.\n- Harbor’s licenses,
          bonds, and financial coverage remain active.\n- Customer funds and outstanding
          obligations remain covered.\n- Harbor can complete reports, refunds, complaints,
          and examinations.\n- Required records remain available.\n- Mosaic’s operational
          role is permitted.\n- The partner bank accepts the structure.\n- Each relevant
          regulator permits or accepts the structure.\n\nThe present plan creates
          tension with this approach. A single Mosaic account, one combined balance,
          and full access to Mosaic products make it harder to show that Harbor remains
          the true provider.\n\n**Partner-bank custody**\n\nA partner bank account
          is not automatically a substitute for a money transmitter license. The key
          questions concern the complete activity and obligation flow.\n\nFor each
          customer balance and transfer, document:\n\n1. Who receives the customer’s
          instruction?\n2. Who accepts the obligation to transmit or return the funds?\n3.
          In whose name is the bank account held?\n4. Is it a custodial or “for benefit
          of” account?\n5. Who can direct withdrawals?\n6. Who owns the ledger and
          resolves errors?\n7. Who bears loss if a transfer fails?\n8. Which entity
          owes the customer a refund?\n9. Which entity’s license, bond, and permissible
          investments cover the obligation?\n10. Does the bank agreement permit assignment,
          migration, or a change in the program manager?\n11. Is bank consent required
          before closing or migration?\n12. What happens to funds if Harbor, Mosaic,
          or the bank relationship ends?\n\nA bank-led model might provide a different
          licensing analysis if the bank is the actual provider and Mosaic performs
          only permitted services. A bank account that merely holds funds for Mosaic
          or Harbor is different. The legal documents, customer terms, control rights,
          and actual operations must all support the claimed model.\n\nAlso review:\n\n-
          account segregation;\n- daily reconciliation;\n- shortfalls and reserve
          funding;\n- bank setoff rights;\n- liens and security interests;\n- continuity
          if the account is frozen;\n- treatment of pending transfers;\n- return and
          chargeback duties;\n- insolvency treatment;\n- customer disclosures; and\n-
          whether any deposit-insurance statement is accurate for the actual account
          structure.\n\n**Recommended closing position**\n\nKeep the acquisition closing
          separate from the regulated-service launch.\n\nFor the four Harbor-only
          states, use a state launch hold unless Mosaic has documented authority.
          For overlapping states, confirm that Mosaic’s existing licenses cover the
          complete post-close product set and funds flow.\n\nDo not surrender Harbor’s
          licenses or release its bonds until the applicable regulators permit it
          and all outstanding obligations have been assigned, completed, or placed
          into an approved run-off structure.\n\nThis investigation does not change
          the current recommendation. It adds one material point: **partner-bank custody
          is part of the licensing analysis, but custody alone does not cure an authority
          gap.**\n\n</details>\n\nResearch history: [Saved research 1](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n\n<!--
          issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045 -->\n### BSA/AML and KYC: whether
          relying on Harbor's prior KYC (with missing underlying documents for pre-2023
          users) satisfies Mosaic Relay's independent CIP/AML obligations\n\nNo separate
          current answer is saved for this issue.\n\nInitial answer — research not
          complete.\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38 -->\n### SAR and
          alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor's ~40 open
          alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n\nNo separate current answer is
          saved for this issue.\n\nInitial answer — research not complete.\n\n<!--
          issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542 -->\n### Monitoring vendor transition:
          continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract terminates at
          close\n\nNo separate current answer is saved for this issue.\n\nInitial
          answer — research not complete.\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66
          -->\n### Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
          money transmission or consumer protection implications\n\nNo separate current
          answer is saved for this issue.\n\nInitial answer — research not complete.\n<!--
          saved-issue-analysis:end -->\n\nDossier preview generated; no matter records
          changed.\n\nIncluded full saved answers for 5 issue(s)."

        available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


          - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
          out).

          - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
          Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and
          full access to Mosaic''s product set.

          - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

          - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay
          holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

          - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
          pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
          onboarded before 2023.

          - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
          terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
          engine on day 1.

          - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
          launching close+1.

          - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last
          year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

          - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
          Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.

          - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were
          already KYC''d.

          - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results
          exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
          before 2023.

          - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
          terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
          engine on day 1.

          - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last
          year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

          - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
          buys Harbor''s assets)

          - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
          institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
          required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

          - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last
          year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

          - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
          Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its
          own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

          - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is
          the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
          and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s
          AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must
          confirm.

          - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been
          reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have
          not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

          - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
          is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding
          those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s
          licenses for the four new markets.


          ## Assumptions


          - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
          Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
          without new state approval

          - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
          Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

          - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and validated
          before close without a monitoring gap

          - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
          MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

          - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41
          states (per the request).

          - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
          which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
          (structure not yet confirmed).'

useful_content: "# Harbor 2 matter dossier\n\n## Current position\n\nThe Harbor Pay
  migration needs legal and compliance review before the targeted Nov 15 close. This
  is the accepted working view, not a recorded decision.\n\nMosaic plans to buy Harbor’s
  assets and move 240,000 consumer users and 12,000 business accounts into one Mosaic
  account on day one. The main obstacles are:\n\n1. Mosaic has not shown that it can
  use Harbor’s licenses in the four Harbor-only states.\n2. Mosaic has not confirmed
  that Harbor’s prior know-your-customer (KYC) results satisfy Mosaic’s anti-money-laundering
  (AML) program.\n3. Harbor’s approximately 40 open alerts and recent suspicious activity
  report (SAR) history remain unread.\n4. The current monitoring service ends at close,
  and the replacement feed has not been shown to work.\n5. The terms of the $50 welcome
  bonus are not known.\n\nThe current direction remains unchanged. A full day-one
  migration is the planning baseline, but the saved working view supports launch restrictions
  where these conditions are not resolved. No decisions are recorded.\n\nThe analysis
  assumes that Harbor and Mosaic conduct regulated money-transmission activity and
  that Mosaic will become the operating provider immediately after close. It does
  not assume that Harbor’s licenses transfer, that Harbor’s KYC records are sufficient,
  or that the monitoring change will work without a gap.\n\nA newer reported answer
  confirms that the deal is an asset purchase. It replaces the earlier assumption
  that the deal structure was unknown.\n\n## Decision question\n\nDoes any part of
  the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close?\n\n##
  Issues\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045 -->\n### Money transmission
  licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined 44-state footprint
  and whether Harbor's MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n\n**Current answer**\n\nMosaic
  should not rely on Harbor’s money transmitter licenses as assets that automatically
  move to Mosaic. Before Mosaic starts regulated services in a state, it needs documented
  authority for the complete post-close activity in that state.\n\nThe asset purchase
  may close separately from the service launch. For the four Harbor-only states, the
  current working position is to hold regulated functions unless Mosaic has its own
  license, required state approval, a supported interim structure, or another documented
  basis to operate.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe saved research concludes that the
  answer must be determined state by state. The review must cover Mosaic’s authority,
  Harbor’s notices or approvals, outstanding obligations, interim operation, and license
  surrender.\n\nFour sources were retrieved, but no relevant passages were read or
  verified. The saved materials therefore do not establish an operative state rule:\n\n-
  [Research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n-
  [CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — retrieved, passage not reviewed](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538-157583424427.md)\n-
  [New York Department of Financial Services licensing page — retrieved, passage not
  reviewed](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4-fa80c95c5393.md)\n\nThe
  model act is not proof of the law in any specific state.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor
  reportedly holds licenses in 38 states. Mosaic reportedly holds licenses in 41 states.
  The proposed combined footprint has 44 states and would open four new markets. Mosaic
  currently plans to use or assume Harbor’s licenses in those markets. The deal is
  an asset purchase.\n\nThe unified Mosaic account, combined balance, and access to
  Mosaic products suggest that Mosaic may become the actual provider. If so, keeping
  Harbor’s entity or licenses active might not give Mosaic authority. A transition
  in which Harbor remains the licensed provider could be possible only if the contracts,
  funds flow, customer terms, operating control, and applicable state requirements
  support that result.\n\nBank custody alone would not establish that Mosaic can perform
  the regulated activity. The full allocation of customer obligations and transfer
  control remains material.\n\n**Next step**\n\nIdentify the four Harbor-only states.
  Prepare one state matrix covering:\n\n- Mosaic’s authority for each post-close activity;\n-
  required transaction notices and approvals;\n- whether interim operation is permitted;\n-
  outstanding customer obligations;\n- bank custody and control;\n- Harbor’s run-off
  duties; and\n- license surrender requirements.\n\nDo not activate regulated functions
  in a state without documented authority.\n\n<!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:start
  -->\n<details>\n<summary>Saved research and prior analysis</summary>\n\nDo not rely
  on transferability without an applicable state rule, approval, or written regulator
  position.\n\nThe answer must be determined state by state and must cover more than
  technical change-of-control rules.\n\nThis path is possible only if Harbor remains
  the real provider and the relevant states permit the arrangement. The unified Mosaic
  account design may conflict with that position.\n\nThe result depends on the contracts
  and actual funds flow. Custody alone should not be treated as a licensing exemption
  or transfer mechanism.\n\nResearch saved. 4 sources retrieved; 0 with passages read.\n\nNext
  step: Identify the four Harbor-only states and complete one matrix covering license
  authority, transaction filings, interim operation, bank custody, outstanding obligations,
  and license surrender.\n\n<details>\n<summary>Detailed analysis</summary>\n\n**Practical
  answer**\n\n**Do not treat Harbor’s money transmitter licenses as assets that move
  to Mosaic in the asset purchase.** Use this closing rule:\n\n> **No confirmed authority
  means no regulated launch by Mosaic in that state.**\n\nThe asset purchase can still
  close. However, Mosaic should not activate regulated services in the four Harbor-only
  states unless one of these conditions is met:\n\n1. Mosaic obtains its own license.\n2.
  The state approves a transfer or other license change.\n3. The regulator confirms
  a lawful interim structure.\n4. Harbor remains the real licensed provider under
  a valid transition plan.\n5. Mosaic blocks regulated functions in that state.\n\nThe
  planned unified Mosaic account is important. It suggests that Mosaic, not Harbor,
  will become the service provider. If that is correct, keeping Harbor’s legal entity
  and licenses alive might not give Mosaic authority to operate.\n\n**No verified
  operative authority retrieved.** The collection found the CSBS Model Money Transmission
  Modernization Act and a New York regulator licensing page. However, no exact provision
  about an asset sale, license transfer, interim operation, or custody was available
  for review. Also, a model act is not proof of the law adopted in a specific state.
  The state-specific conclusions below remain conditional.\n\n**Work needed before
  launch**\n\n| Work | Why | Proposed owner | Needed by | Evidence to proceed | Fallback
  |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Identify the four Harbor-only states | These states
  have the clearest authority gap | Licensing team | Now | Confirmed license list
  and covered activities | Block regulated functions in those states |\n| Build a
  matrix for every affected state | Transfer, notice, approval, and surrender rules
  can differ | State regulatory counsel | Before the closing conditions are final
  | Applicable rule, filing deadline, regulator response, and license status | Delay
  migration in the affected state |\n| Confirm the post-close service provider | The
  licensed entity must match the actual operating model | Product and deal counsel
  | Before customer notices and account design are final | Contracts, user interface,
  funds-flow diagram, and operating roles | Keep Harbor as the actual provider where
  permitted |\n| Review notices and approvals | An asset sale can create separate
  seller and buyer requirements | Licensing team | Before each state deadline | Filing
  receipts and required approvals or non-objections | Make approval a state launch
  condition |\n| Confirm interim operating authority | A pending application should
  not be assumed to permit operation | State regulatory counsel | Before close | Applicable
  rule or written regulator confirmation | Keep Harbor customers segregated or restrict
  transactions |\n| Review partner-bank arrangements | Bank custody does not, by itself,
  establish Mosaic’s licensing position | Payments counsel and bank relationship owner
  | Before balances move | Bank agreements, account titles, control rights, reconciliation
  design, and bank consent | Keep funds and obligations in the existing structure
  |\n| Prepare license run-off and surrender plans | Harbor may retain duties for
  balances, claims, records, and reports | Harbor compliance and deal counsel | Before
  surrender or operational shutdown | Regulator-approved plan and continued bonds
  and financial coverage | Keep Harbor licensed and operational longer |\n\n**State
  notice and approval**\n\nDo not search only for a rule called “license transfer.”
  Review each state for:\n\n- sale of substantially all assets;\n- change of control;\n-
  change in business plan;\n- change in licensed activities;\n- assignment of outstanding
  payment obligations;\n- change in responsible persons, locations, or agents;\n-
  license surrender or termination;\n- customer agreement assignment; and\n- movement
  of stored balances or customer funds.\n\nAn asset purchase might fall outside a
  technical “change of control” rule because Harbor’s ownership does not change. That
  does not resolve the issue. Harbor might still need a notice or surrender approval.
  Mosaic might separately need authority before it starts the regulated activity.\n\nThe
  state matrix should distinguish:\n\n- notice only;\n- approval before closing;\n-
  approval before customer migration;\n- new license required;\n- operation permitted
  while an application is pending;\n- regulator-approved transition available; and\n-
  no supported interim path.\n\n**Interim operation**\n\nHarbor could remain the licensed
  provider for a transition period. However, the structure must be real, not only
  contractual language.\n\nA supportable structure would normally need to show that:\n\n-
  Harbor remains responsible to customers.\n- Customer terms name Harbor as the provider.\n-
  Harbor controls the regulated activity as required.\n- Harbor’s licenses, bonds,
  and financial coverage remain active.\n- Customer funds and outstanding obligations
  remain covered.\n- Harbor can complete reports, refunds, complaints, and examinations.\n-
  Required records remain available.\n- Mosaic’s operational role is permitted.\n-
  The partner bank accepts the structure.\n- Each relevant regulator permits or accepts
  the structure.\n\nThe present plan creates tension with this approach. A single
  Mosaic account, one combined balance, and full access to Mosaic products make it
  harder to show that Harbor remains the true provider.\n\n**Partner-bank custody**\n\nA
  partner bank account is not automatically a substitute for a money transmitter license.
  The key questions concern the complete activity and obligation flow.\n\nFor each
  customer balance and transfer, document:\n\n1. Who receives the customer’s instruction?\n2.
  Who accepts the obligation to transmit or return the funds?\n3. In whose name is
  the bank account held?\n4. Is it a custodial or “for benefit of” account?\n5. Who
  can direct withdrawals?\n6. Who owns the ledger and resolves errors?\n7. Who bears
  loss if a transfer fails?\n8. Which entity owes the customer a refund?\n9. Which
  entity’s license, bond, and permissible investments cover the obligation?\n10. Does
  the bank agreement permit assignment, migration, or a change in the program manager?\n11.
  Is bank consent required before closing or migration?\n12. What happens to funds
  if Harbor, Mosaic, or the bank relationship ends?\n\nA bank-led model might provide
  a different licensing analysis if the bank is the actual provider and Mosaic performs
  only permitted services. A bank account that merely holds funds for Mosaic or Harbor
  is different. The legal documents, customer terms, control rights, and actual operations
  must all support the claimed model.\n\nAlso review:\n\n- account segregation;\n-
  daily reconciliation;\n- shortfalls and reserve funding;\n- bank setoff rights;\n-
  liens and security interests;\n- continuity if the account is frozen;\n- treatment
  of pending transfers;\n- return and chargeback duties;\n- insolvency treatment;\n-
  customer disclosures; and\n- whether any deposit-insurance statement is accurate
  for the actual account structure.\n\n**Recommended closing position**\n\nKeep the
  acquisition closing separate from the regulated-service launch.\n\nFor the four
  Harbor-only states, use a state launch hold unless Mosaic has documented authority.
  For overlapping states, confirm that Mosaic’s existing licenses cover the complete
  post-close product set and funds flow.\n\nDo not surrender Harbor’s licenses or
  release its bonds until the applicable regulators permit it and all outstanding
  obligations have been assigned, completed, or placed into an approved run-off structure.\n\nThis
  investigation does not change the current recommendation. It adds one material point:
  **partner-bank custody is part of the licensing analysis, but custody alone does
  not cure an authority gap.**\n\n</details>\n\nResearch history: [Saved research
  1](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n\n</details>\n<!--
  retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:end -->\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045
  -->\n### BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor's prior KYC (with missing underlying
  documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay's independent CIP/AML obligations\n\n**Current
  answer**\n\nThe current no-reverification plan is not yet supported. Mosaic’s compliance
  team has not confirmed that its AML and customer identification program permits
  reliance on Harbor’s prior KYC results.\n\nThe missing documents prove a record
  gap. They do not, by themselves, prove that identification was not completed or
  that a violation occurred.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nThe applicable rule depends
  on Mosaic’s legal status, its AML program, the permitted form of reliance, and the
  records that must remain available. This issue has not been researched. No saved
  authority establishes that Harbor’s pass/fail results are sufficient or insufficient.\n\n**Application**\n\nHarbor’s
  KYC vendor closed in 2024. Mosaic has pass/fail results for all users but lacks
  underlying documents for users onboarded before 2023. Mosaic plans to migrate the
